transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2027-03-16 14:00 UTC | Duration: 62 minutes | Attendees: Ava Martinez, Liam Chen, Priya Rao (Redwood) and Sofia Patel, Marcus Vogel, Ines Duarte, Tomás Ribeiro (HelioCore)

Summary: Quick check-in on upcoming renewal window; HelioCore is considering a 30% uplift on committed vCPU/GPU hours, exploring EU on-prem path for data residency, and asking for a pilot to validate latency and throughput. Redwood AE/SE pair covering pricing, canary and onprem rollout options.

Topics: commitment uplift, burst capacity windows, EU private/on-prem pathway, KMS & audit logs, SOC2 & ISO, SSO/SAML, throughput and latency SLOs, fallback routing to hosted.

Action items (spoken): Ava will send amended commitment, Liam to run benchmarks, Ines to send audit fields, Tomás to share infra details.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on — can hear me okay?
[00:06] Sofia Patel: Yup, loud and clear. Hey Ava, thanks. We've got Marcus, Ines and Tomás on our side.
[00:11] Marcus Vogel: Hi. Quick agenda — renewal terms, extra capacity, and then the EU on-prem option we poked at in the RFP.
[00:18] Ava Martinez: Perfect. We'll do high-level then get into the pilot plan. Liam, do you want to call out the benchmark ask?
[00:24] Liam Chen: Sure. For the private pilot we recommend a 48-hour benchmark that covers 95th/99th p99 latency at our usual seq lengths. We'll run both a quantized LLM variant and an FP16 variant to show cost vs latency. We also want to exercise KV cache warmup and prefix cache — that impacts throughput a lot.
[00:40] Tomás Ribeiro: Quick Q — on the on-prem option, are we talking full on-prem control plane or just a VPC-resident runtime? We have some airgap constraints.
[00:47] Liam Chen: So Redwood Private supports two modes. There's a customer-managed control plane which is the VPC-hosted control plane, and there's the on-prem package which is the full offline option. Note: the on-prem installer currently needs sudo-level access and we've seen teams take a week for infra prep.
[01:02] Ines Duarte: On the security side, we need explicit audit logs for per-token processing (or at least request IDs + model version mappings) and KMS integration for keys. Can you confirm HSM-level compatibility?
[01:12] Priya Rao: We support KMS integrations and HSM is supported via our enterprise connectors; I'll share the integration note. For audit logs the platform emits request-level metadata, but I want to flag that per-token content logging is something we don't store by default for privacy reasons.
[01:28] Marcus Vogel: That's fine, we only need the lineage — model version, prompt hash, timestamp, route and tenant id.
[01:33] Ava Martinez: We'll put that into the SOW for the pilot. On commitments, I know you mentioned a 30% uplift — are you targeting additional dedicated capacity or more burstable minutes on Hosted?
[01:44] Sofia Patel: Good question. We're leaning to a mix: dedicated reserved capacity for steady state and a burst bucket for Black Friday-like spikes. Ideally EU-located capacity for data sovereignty.
[01:56] Liam Chen: For the steady state we recommend Redwood Dedicated with a reserved GPU pool + a configured autoscale policy. For spikes we can attach burst capacity from our shared pools — tradeoff is a looser latency SLA during spikes if you use shared burst.
[02:12] Tomás Ribeiro: Latency tradeoff — can you give numbers? We're currently targeting 80 ms median token latency with a p95 under 300 ms at our seq 512 workload.
[02:23] Liam Chen: On our EU Dedicated instance with A100-ish profiles we see medians in the 60–90 ms range for causal decoding at seq512 for the LLM family you referenced. But the quantized int8 paths can reduce cost by ~2x with a p99 penalty sometimes. There's also compilation kernels that behave differently on different GPUs; we'll include a hardware matrix.
[02:44] Ines Duarte: Regarding SOC2, ISO — can we get copies of current attestations? We need them for procurement.
[02:50] Ava Martinez: Absolutely. We'll share SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs. Priya will drop those.
[02:56] Priya Rao: I'll DM links after the call, and include our KMS/HSM integration docs and the audit log CSV schema.
[03:05] Marcus Vogel: About the on-prem pilot — our infra team is concerned about ingress/egress. If the private runtime needs outbound connectivity for updates, that won't work for our air-gapped lab.
[03:15] Liam Chen: For fully air-gapped installs, our on-prem package can be bundled with a static bundle; however updates are manual. The control plane features like rollouts and metrics need a control path; for the fully air-gapped customers we recommend local Grafana+Prometheus ingestion and S3-compatible object store for model assets. It's doable, but increases ops overhead.
[03:36] Tomás Ribeiro: That overhead is expected. We need clear runbook and a checklist. Can you provide a runbook and preflight checklist?
[03:43] Ava Martinez: Yes. Liam, you have the preflight checklist?
[03:46] Liam Chen: I do. I'll attach the runbook and preflight verbatim to the pilot ticket. It includes network ports, kernel driver versions, CUDA/ROCm versions, NVMe sizing for KV cache, and expected node sizing.
[03:59] Sofia Patel: For pricing, if we commit to 12 months at +30% capacity, what's the unit discount and how do burst credits factor into invoicing?
[04:08] Ava Martinez: We can present two options in the revised quote: (A) reserved capacity with a 15% unit discount + 10% allocation for burst as pre-purchased credits, (B) larger reserved with smaller burst but layered discounts tied to annual commit. We'll include explicit billing examples.
[04:21] Marcus Vogel: Are there penalties if we exceed the burst allocation? We want predictable overruns.
[04:26] Ava Martinez: Overages are billed at a higher overage rate; we can also do an auto-top-up policy that notifies you at 80% consumption and allows a safety top-up to avoid throttling. That can be codified in the SOW.
[04:40] Ines Duarte: One more from security: SSO/SAML and RBAC. Can we map our IdP groups to Redwood roles?
[04:47] Priya Rao: Yes, SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning plus fine-grained RBAC is supported. We'll share a role mapping example.
[04:55] Tomás Ribeiro: For the benchmark — what telemetry will you collect? We need consistent sampling so we can compare p95/p99 numbers.
[05:02] Liam Chen: We'll export token latency histogram, model version, GPU utilization, memory churn, batch size distribution, KV cache hit ratio, and network I/O. We'll provide the raw CSV so you can run your own analysis.
[05:14] Sofia Patel: Perfect. Also, one of our concerns: fallback routing. If EU capacity is saturated, will requests route to US-hosted? That's a data residency no-no for some tenants.
[05:25] Ava Martinez: Fallback policies are configurable per-tenant and per-route. We can enforce strict residency for regulated traffic and allow broader routing for less-sensitive, fallback to hosted as long as you opt-in. We'll call that out in the policy settings.
[05:39] Marcus Vogel: Timeline — our renewal window opens 2027-04-01. We need signed amendment before then ideally. Can you meet that?
[05:47] Ava Martinez: Yes, we'll prioritize. I'll send the amendment by Thu 3/18 and then schedule the pilot for the week of 3/22.
[05:53] Ines Duarte: One small gotcha — for our procurement we need to see sample audit logs and a list of retained fields. Please include retention periods.
[06:01] Priya Rao: We'll include that. Default retention for request metadata in the dedicated product is 90 days, with configurable longer retention as an add-on.
[06:10] Tomás Ribeiro: Lastly, micro detail on model versions: when you say "model variant", can you pin both the model hash and inference compiler version so we can reproduce results?
[06:19] Liam Chen: Absolutely. We use a model artifact hash and runtime build id. The pilot SOW will include exact image tags and compiler flags.
[06:27] Sofia Patel: Great. Anything else?
[06:29] Ava Martinez: Not for me. Quick recap: we'll send docs (SOC2/ISO/KMS), revised price/commitment options by 3/18, run a 48-hour benchmark w/c 3/22, provide runbooks and audit log schema, and customer to share infra specs and QPS numbers.
[06:44] Marcus Vogel: Sounds good. Thank you all.
[06:47] Ava Martinez: Thanks team, we'll follow up in email with artifacts.
[06:50] Call ends.

Notes about transcript: occasional mis-hearings present — e.g., "kernels" transcribed as "carols" in one snippet of the raw audio, and brand mentions like "Redwood Dedicated" sometimes appear as "Redwood Dedicatedy" in the auto captions. Those artifacts were cleaned lightly but some remain to preserve authenticity.
